_readme: Every state (plus DC) classified by what vacancy data it publishes, and why it is or is not on the dashboard. 'checked' = 'direct' when this project read the primary source; 'lpi' when the classification relies on the Learning Policy Institute's July 2026 scan (Tan, Baez & Patrick, 'State Teacher Shortages 2026 Update'); 'secondary' when only news or third-party coverage was reachable. Re-check annually.

base_source.label: Learning Policy Institute, State Teacher Shortages 2026 Update (July 2026)

categories.candidate: Publishes a rate or a same-source denominator, but not added yet (reason given)
categories.counts: Publishes vacancy counts only; no denominator from the same source
categories.different: Publishes a figure that measures something different (e.g., includes uncertified teachers or counts job postings)
categories.none: No statewide vacancy data published (per LPI 2026)

states.what: Oct 1 unfilled FTE by category with filled FTE; published rate
states.reason: Start-of-year snapshot with a same-source denominator, multi-year.

states.what: Fall unfilled FTE / total available FTE (published rate)
states.reason: Start-of-year snapshot, published rate, multi-year.

states.what: Beginning-of-year vacancies and authorized FTE (CERRA)
states.reason: Start-of-year snapshot with same-source denominator; includes service staff (flagged).

states.what: 12-month count of full-time postings unfilled or filled by substitutes, / employed teachers
states.reason: Published rate, multi-year; shown as a different measure.

states.what: Positions unfilled all year / all teaching positions
states.reason: Published rate, multi-year; shown as a different measure.

states.what: Vacant and 'unfilled' counts (no denominator)
states.reason: Shown as counts only; illustrates vacant vs. not-fully-qualified.

states.what: Fall share of teaching FTE 'vacant' from state personnel records (EPIC/MSU statutory report): 2.8% in fall 2024
states.reason: The closest additional candidate. But 'vacancy' includes positions temporarily covered by substitutes or held for staff on leave, and districts were only required to report vacancies from 2023-24, so only one or two years are reliable and the 2023-24 statewide rate is published only in a chart. Revisit when the January 2027 report adds fall 2025.

states.what: OSSE fall Faculty & Staff collection: vacant teacher FTE (193.5 in 2025-26; 362 in 2023-24) and teacher headcounts (9,145; 8,767)
states.reason: A rate can be computed from the same collection (about 2.1% and 4.0%), but vacancies are FTE and teachers are headcounts, OSSE does not publish a rate, and a city-district is not a state. Could be added with those caveats.

states.what: ADE fall survey: about 4,200 teacher positions vacant or covered by stopgaps; about 1,400 completely unfilled (reported as about 2.4% of positions in 2025-26 vs. 2.8% the prior year)
states.reason: ADE's report blocks automated access and the percentages could only be confirmed in news coverage. Needs the primary report; a person can download it.

states.what: TDOE Educator Vacancy Report: 1,009 (2022-23), 1,434 (2023-24), about 817-831 (2024-25) teaching positions not filled by a licensed teacher for 20+ days
states.reason: Definition includes positions covered by substitutes; a statewide rate ('just under 2%' for 2023-24) appears only in secondary coverage. The State Board PDF could not be retrieved automatically.

states.what: Hiring-practices survey: 259 instructional and non-instructional positions unfilled at end of hiring season, about 2.5% of the workforce
states.reason: Pools non-instructional staff, end-of-hiring-season timing, survey of HR leads, and no consistent multi-year series.

states.what: MSDE Annual Vacancy Data Collection: 1,615 (2021-22) to 886.2 (2025-26) teacher vacancies
states.reason: Counts only; no published rate or same-source denominator.

states.what: PDE professional vacancies (teachers, administrators, counselors), October and quarterly; flags long-term substitutes
states.reason: Counts only, pools professional roles; collection changed to quarterly in 2024-25.

states.what: Superintendents' association survey: teacher and staff vacancies at start of year, 2021-2025
states.reason: Counts from an association survey, not a state agency; no denominator.

states.what: 671 teacher vacancies as of Sept 1 (Superintendent webcast)
states.reason: Counts only, presented in a webcast.

states.what: 656 FTE unfilled teacher positions, October (DESE Educator Vacancy Report)
states.reason: Counts only; report not retrievable automatically.

states.what: 795 unfilled teacher positions in August (Educator Vacancy Dashboard)
states.reason: Counts; August timing; interactive dashboard.

states.what: 324 teacher positions unfilled on the first day of school (dashboard)
states.reason: Counts only.

states.what: 219 unfilled FTE teaching positions in fall (university system survey)
states.reason: Counts only; new collection.

states.what: 137 unfilled FTE instructional staff positions at start of year (turnover and vacancy dashboard)
states.reason: Counts; instructional staff; dashboard only.

states.what: 3,815 unfilled teacher positions reported by districts in fall 2025
states.reason: Counts only.

states.what: 205 unfilled teaching positions in November (school boards association survey)
states.reason: Association survey; counts only.

states.what: 2,260 unfilled teacher positions at start of 2025-26 (teachers' union compilation of district data)
states.reason: Not a state-agency figure; counts only.

states.what: 294 teacher positions being recruited for as of September 2023
states.reason: Single-year count; dated.

states.what: 736 unfilled teacher positions, 2024-25
states.reason: Counts only.

states.what: 1,039 education positions to be filled before 2023-24
states.reason: Pools non-teaching roles; dated.

states.what: 1,747 'vacancies' in fall 2025
states.reason: Kansas counts positions filled by educators not fully certified as vacancies.

states.what: 1,684 positions in shortage areas not filled with certified teachers (December)
states.reason: Includes positions filled by long-term substitutes or emergency-certified teachers; shortage areas only.

states.what: 2,881 positions not filled by a contracted full-time teacher, reported at year end
states.reason: End-of-year measure that includes positions covered by substitutes.

states.what: 604 open teacher job postings in September (university vacancy report)
states.reason: Counts advertised postings, which may overstate vacancies.
